title: Daniel:
headline: A donor's rule for life, “start with one”, is the same idea as Watsi: one patient, one person you can name.
story: Daniel asks founders one question: name one person you have really helped. Most can't. His rule: before you change the world for millions, start with one. He lives it. He once gave a spare laptop to his Uber driver who wanted to learn to code. The student chapter he started 13 years ago is still going.

Then he connects it to Watsi: you don't see “global health”, you see one child, one mother, one father, and you think: that could be my family. He ends on a hopeful note: anyone can give. Time, a referral, a minute. Person first. Watsi comes in the last third.
do: Open on frame 1 with Daniel's own question line. Top text: <q>Name one person.</q>
Name super “Daniel” only, large, after the hook line.
Let the laptop story play as one piece. It is the proof of the rule.
Use Nick's question as top text before the last answer: <q>Do you have to feel wealthy to give?</q>
End on watsi.org, lowercase. Nothing else on the end card.
dont: Don't open on “Watsi is a platform that…”. Watsi comes in the last third.
No company names, no pitch, no “Silicon Valley” lines.
No hero music, no slow-motion “philanthropist” look.
No Medellín or hospital B-roll. Only Sept 22 NYC footage.
